reviews.title: AI cat vibes meets pseudo-positive psychology startup
reviews.text: I wanted to like this app.  I REALLY wanted to love it-- it's the first of its kind that's actually affordable 💥 but, unfortunately, it just felt like an endless horribly-gamified tutorial.  After each step of the setup, you have to watch a dumb, unskippable, animation of a cat dancing with imaginary points that rack up like you're giving a Google Maps review or something.  Then there's the infinite, unskippable AI chat bot tutorial.   Even though EVERY SINGLE AI EXPERT EVER says to not use AI for emotional support, this app basically forces the user to go down this dark path.  Look, I'm glad it helps others, but, as someone who was unable to complete the tutorial, I really don't recommend this app.  It feels disrespectful to my time.

reviews.title: Overall great
reviews.text:
This app is targeted for people who are feeling rock bottom with little direction or motivation to take action in their life. I chose the gamification option and find it cute. There’s a cute celebration animation when you earn points doing various activities.

The audio in this app is better than most. I have a lifetime sub to Calm and I find that it often falls short. The soundscapes and nature sounds are really nice, and I love that binaural beats are included. 

I also love the goal section, where you break your goals down into smaller, actionable chunks, and it seemingly randomly assigns point values to them. So you have to break them up accordingly, or just deal with the randomness. It’s a nice UI.

The life wheel assessment is also great. You choose what your wheel is composed of and can reassess whenever.

There’s all AI chat which is pretty good. I don’t rly use AI but honestly this one is well-suited for functionality within the app. I feel like the people who designed this app really know their stuff and have good taste.

One major thing I would recommend is a way to spend your points and being able to build a cozy home or customize an avatar or something. 

I haven’t unlocked all the levels so maybe that is available.

reviews.title: I really like this app. And therapist too!
reviews.text: I really like this app it feels like a buddy I can check in with when I need guidance on what to do with my day, to feel better, etc. It’s hard to describe this app in a nutshell but even my therapist asked me to send her the babe after I had described it and how I’ve been using it. Most habit tracking apps I abandon after a few days or weeks because of my adhd, but with Shmoody I haven’t. I think it’s low key enough that I don’t feel pressure or guilt, just that Shmoody is a resource for my self-care to-to list, ideas from the chat bit, checking in, organizing thoughts, etc. I can use whichever features are helpful for me that day.

reviews.title: Insight
reviews.text: Shmoody is a great app because it enables me to “face” my mood & what I am feeling in a neutral setting.  Otherwise, it is too easy to ignore my feelings which leads to my negative moods.  Shmoody allows me to think- in a subtle reminder.

reviews.title: Genuinely Helpful Affordable Mental Health Tool
reviews.text:
This app is right for you if you’re looking for:
1.) An app that’s easily integrated into your daily routine, isn’t overwhelming, & actually does help 
2.) A company that genuinely cares about your individual journey, wants to see you improve, & is dedicated to the affordability of mental health tools

⚠️ There’s an option for a low cost free trial, which can be extended far past a week - go through the prompts after your trial week expires!! 😉
I did a trial & found the interface to be user-friendly, the daily tasks and journaling were very helpful, & overall I felt it was a great app for trying to get on top of things. Because it wasn’t overwhelming, like some can be, it didn’t put me off from doing things I knew I needed to.

Unfortunately I have some complications that made it difficult for me to incorporate the app into my life and I definitely wish I would’ve had the time to do things properly, but when I was able to use the app it was a fantastic experience.
